guidebook.intro: Elders end arguments with a proverb, and kangas carry them on their hems. Knowing a few marks you as someone who really speaks Swahili.

phrases.base: Little by little fills the measure.

tips.title: Always true: hu-
body: Proverbs use **hu-** for things that always happen: **hujaza** (fills), **huvunjika** (gets broken). It has no person prefix: **hu-** works for everyone.
You’ll hear it for habits too: **Mimi hunywa chai asubuhi** (I usually drink tea in the morning).

culture.title: Proverbs on kangas
body: A kanga’s message is often a proverb. A woman might wear **Haba na haba hujaza kibaba** to say she is patient, or something sharper to answer a neighbour’s gossip.
